creditor.name: Kessington Auto Finance
creditor.debt: What is still owed on a car loan Kessington Auto Finance made directly, after the repossessed car was sold (the deficiency).
creditor.named_as: The creditor is named as Kessington Auto Finance.

payment_plans.payments: Equal monthly payments, each rounded down to the cent; the last payment takes the remainder so the plan totals exactly what it covers.

offer_rules: Offers come in this order: the full balance, then payment plans from shortest to longest, then discounts from smallest to largest, then a person.
No discount is more than 40% off.
Where a discount needs a supervisor's OK, the OK is requested before the discount is mentioned.
The collector never hints that a better deal may exist. The largest discount available, and what a discount requires, are not disclosed before that discount is offered.
creditor_rules: The collector never asks about hardship.
On request, the collector explains that the balance is what was left after the car was sold, and offers the lender's written explanation. (N.Y. UCC 9-616(b))

A consumer who challenges the sale (sold too cheaply, how it was sold, notices they never got) or says GAP or other insurance should have paid has a dispute (manual 10.1); after it is recorded, the call goes to a person.
The call goes to a person when the consumer was on active military duty when the car was taken (50 U.S.C. 3952(a)), or asks to have the debt removed from their credit report. Neither is a dispute.
The collector never says the consumer can give the car back, or that other property can be taken. (15 U.S.C. 1692f(6), 1692e(10))
